What comes up in Avoca Beach

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. What follows is how this work normally runs in the area, not a reading of any one block.

Original fibro beach house

The commonest Avoca Beach job, and the sheeting sets the programme.

How it is handled
Condition assessed, removed under licence sheet by sheet rather than broken, then independent clearance before demolition starts.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, then a small machine once clearance is issued.

Steep block with no street room

Where both the driveway and the kerb are constraints at the same time.

How it is handled
Material moved up the block in stages and loaded at the street in sequenced loads rather than stockpiled.
What does it
Mini excavator, hand tools, bogie tippers staged at the street.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Avoca Beach

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Holiday era fibro housing Much of it never reclad, which puts the sheeting at the front of the scope.
  • Steep coastal blocks Where the driveway decides what plant can get on.
  • Narrow streets with no room to stand So material leaves in sequenced loads rather than waiting in a stockpile.
  • Heavy coastal weathering Which can move sheeting from bonded to friable and change the controls entirely.

Avoca Beach combines the two hardest constraints on this coast: a steep block and a street with nowhere to stand. Smaller plant, more passes and material loaded at the street are the usual answer, and it is priced that way rather than discovered.

Avoca Beach questions

What people ask before we start

The house is original 1960s fibro. What does that mean for the job?
It means the sheeting comes out first, under licence, with independent clearance before the structure is touched. Weathering decides whether it is handled as bonded or friable, and that assessment is made on site.
Can anything get down our driveway?
That is the first thing we look at. Where a machine cannot, the work goes to hand demolition with material carried out, which is slower and is quoted that way.
Does sandy ground change how an excavation is done?
Yes. Sandy material drains well and batters poorly, so a face that has to stand is battered back or supported rather than left vertical, and near the water the water table is close enough that dewatering is planned rather than discovered.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
